text:
Detroit's night turned on a 32-minute stretch in which a one-goal Ottawa lead became a 4-1 Red Wings cushion. Tim Stützle scored at 2:44 of the first, and Alex DeBrincat answered 32 seconds later. Dylan Larkin made it 2-1 in the first period, Viktor Arvidsson scored on the power play early in the second, and Justin Faulk made it 4-1 at 4:30 on a wrist shot that carried only a 12 percent chance of scoring. The Senators never saw the lead again.

The numbers say Detroit earned most of it. The Red Wings finished with 3.56 expected goals to Ottawa's 2.62, outattempted them 63 to 52, and won 64 percent of simulated replays of every shot. The first two periods were lopsided in quality: Detroit led 1.33 to 0.45 in the first and 1.52 to 0.98 in the second. At even strength the gap was 1.98 to 1.18. Lucas Raymond had a hand in three goals and put six shots on net, though he never scored.

Ottawa nearly turned it around late. Drake Batherson scored on a power play at 6:08 of the second, and William Eklund cut it to 4-3 at 10:30 of the third, when the Senators produced 1.19 expected goals to Detroit's 0.71 in the period. But Ottawa took 18 penalty minutes, Detroit went 2 for 5 on the power play, and DeBrincat finished it with a power-play goal at 19:10, an 8 percent chance that made it 5-3. Neither goalie stole anything: John Gibson was 0.38 goals below expected, Samuel Ersson 0.53 below.
